dimensions.assessment: Affects U.S. diplomatic and financial engagement at the International Monetary Fund regarding China.
dimensions.evidence: oppose any quota increase at the International Monetary Fund for member countries that employ certain exchange rate practices

dimensions.assessment: Directs formal U.S. opposition to IMF voting power increases for the People's Republic of China under specified conditions.
dimensions.evidence: instruct the Governor of the Fund to use the voice and vote of the United States to oppose the proposal to increase the voting power of the People's Republic of China

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue impacts are stated.
Amends the Bretton Woods Agreements Act to add reporting and voting instruction requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The Bretton Woods Agreements Act (22 U.S.C. 286-286aaa) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Includes a sunset provision taking effect 7 years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall cease to have force or effect 7 years after the date of the enactment of this section.

missing_information: Potential diplomatic or economic retaliation from other IMF member nations.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the U.S. Secretary of the Treasury to make specific determinations regarding China's exchange rate practices and use the U.S. vote and voice at the IMF to oppose quota or voting power increases for China if criteria are not met.
